docs.title: Masader
docs.text:
Masader turns a research question about recent events into a short English brief in which every finding carries an evidence label (corroborated, single-source, disputed, insufficient) and links to the source passages it rests on. A rules layer and an output validator check every sentence against the cited evidence before the brief is delivered. Reviewers approve publication; corrections create new versions.

Links: GitHub repository · release v1.0.0 (docker pull ghcr.io/maryamrra90-create/masader:1.0.0) · documentation site · CI runs · engineering toolchain

This repository is the course implementation of the Masader Proposal (19 Oct 2026) and Technical Architecture v1.2 (28 Oct 2026). Differences from the architecture are listed with reasons in docs/deviations.md.

Important: what is real and what is simulated. By default (MODEL_MODE=simulated) every model call is answered by a deterministic heuristic simulator, not by Claude. The simulator reads the real stage inputs and returns schema-valid output, so the whole system (queues, leases, budgets, rules, validator, rendering, recovery) runs for real, but the wording and judgement in simulated briefs are not model outputs. Simulated runs record model names as sim:<model> and every simulated brief shows a banner. The evaluation corpus is synthetic: 37 items from fictional outlets marked "(fixture)". MODEL_MODE=live uses the Anthropic API through the same gateway; it is implemented but has not been run against the real API in this build.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Source: docs/architecture.mmd. A request goes through eight stages, each a Celery task that takes an atomic claim on its report_stages row, does its work, and commits its rows in the same transaction, fenced on its lease:

collect → dedup → extract → verify → label → write → validate → render

  • cpu stages (worker-cpu): collect (hybrid keyword + vector retrieval), dedup (exact, near-duplicate and origin grouping), label (evidence rules rules-1.1.1), render (JSON + HTML).
  • llm stages (worker-llm): extract claims, verify them against other sources, write the brief, validate every sentence (rule checks + an independent support check by a different model than the writer).
  • gateway: every call reserves its worst-case cost first (a database CHECK makes overspending impossible), retries once on fast errors, repairs invalid JSON once, falls back to a second model, opens a circuit breaker after 5 failures, and can cancel or abandon stuck calls.
  • reaper (beat, every 60 s): recovers expired leases, lost calls and stuck reports.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Requirements: Python 3.12 or 3.13, PostgreSQL 16 with the pgvector extension, Redis 7. Docker is the easiest way to get the two services.

git clone <this repository> masader && cd masader
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt     # all versions are pinned
make services        # starts pgvector/pgvector:pg16 on :5432 and redis:7.4-alpine on :6379

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Settings come from environment variables (see .env.example); the defaults suit local development with make services.

Variable Default Meaning DATABASE_URL postgresql://masader:masader@localhost:5432/masader PostgreSQL with pgvector REDIS_URL redis://localhost:6379/0 broker and rate limits MODEL_MODE simulated simulated (no key, heuristic outputs) or live (Anthropic API) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY empty only for live; keep it in .env or a secret manager, never in Git KEY_PEPPER dev value HMAC pepper for stored API keys; must be set when ENV=prod EMBEDDER hashing hashing (offline substitute) or fastembed (multilingual MiniLM, downloads a model) LIVE_SOURCES 0 1 schedules the real GDELT, RSS and World Bank connectors SIM_LATENCY_SCALE 0 simulated call latency = the role's time budget in minutes × this many seconds ADMISSION_MAX_ACTIVE 6 reports in progress before new requests get 429 busy

Model routing, budgets, evidence-rule thresholds and the source register are in config/. The timers must keep the order call timeout < stage deadline < soft limit < hard limit < lease < visibility timeout (110 < 234 < 240 < 270 < 300 < 360 s); the app refuses to start otherwise.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
make migrate seed                       # schema, sources, budgets, synthetic corpus
python -m masader.cli key create "Me" me@example.org admin --rate 100    # prints an API key once
make run                                # API + UI on http://127.0.0.1:8000
make worker                             # in a second terminal
make beat                               # in a third terminal (reaper, retention)

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000, paste the key, and press Request brief. The form is pre-filled with the corpus example (shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, 12–19 Oct 2026).

docs.title: Use the API
docs.text:
The contract is docs/openapi.v1.json (also live at /docs). Every /v1 route needs X-API-Key. Keys have one of three roles: requester, reviewer, admin.

KEY=rq_...   # your key
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/requests -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
    "topic": "Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz",
    "questions": ["What has happened to commercial shipping in the last 7 days, and how have Gulf and Indian officials responded?"],
    "from": "2026-10-12", "to": "2026-10-19", "geography": ["OMN","ARE","IND"]}'
# -> {"status":"needs_clarification","questions":[...],"answers_url":"/v1/requests/req_.../answers"}

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/requests/req_.../answers -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
# -> 202 {"report_id":"rep_...","status":"queued","status_url":"/v1/reports/rep_..."}   ({} accepts the defaults)

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/reports/rep_... -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"        # status, stages, then the brief
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/reports/rep_....html -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" > brief.html
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/reports/rep_.../publish -H "X-API-Key: $REVIEWER_KEY"   # public at /r/rep_...

Other routes: GET /v1/review/queue and POST /v1/review/{id} (reviewers), POST /v1/reports/{id}/corrections and POST /v1/corrections/{id}/resolve (a correction creates version n+1), POST /v1/reports/{id}/withdraw, GET /v1/me, POST|DELETE /v1/keys, /healthz, /readyz, /metrics.

Command line (python -m masader.cli ...): migrate, seed [--fixtures], key create|revoke, delete-user EMAIL, reap, retention, openapi.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
make test-fast     # unit + AI regression tests, no services needed
make test          # everything: unit, integration (PostgreSQL + Redis) and end-to-end
make cov           # with coverage
make lint
make security      # bandit (static analysis) and pip-audit (known-vulnerable dependencies)

Tests create and drop their own database masader_test and use Redis database 15, so they do not touch development data. The end-to-end tests (tests/e2e) start real Uvicorn, Celery worker and beat processes, kill a worker with SIGKILL mid-stage, hang a call thread that ignores cancellation, and hang a stage past its soft limit, and check that the report is still delivered exactly once.

docs.title: Quality gates in CI and on GitHub
docs.text:
Every push and pull request runs, in GitHub Actions: pre-commit hooks (make precommit: ruff, gitleaks, YAML/JSON/whitespace checks), a gitleaks scan of the whole history, ruff, bandit, pip-audit, the test suite with an 80% coverage floor, the OpenAPI contract diff, the Docker image build and smoke test, a Trivy scan of the image and of the Dockerfile/Compose file (fails on fixable HIGH or CRITICAL findings), and a CycloneDX SBOM of the image (kept as a build artifact). CodeQL code scanning runs on push, pull request and weekly; Dependabot opens weekly update pull requests for pip, GitHub Actions and the Docker base image.

  • Releases: pushing a tag v*, publishing a GitHub release, or running the release workflow by hand publishes the image to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/maryamrra90-create/masader) with a signed build-provenance attestation, an SBOM attestation and a GitHub release (.github/workflows/release.yml).
  • Documentation site: https://maryamrra90-create.github.io/masader/ (MkDocs, built from this README and docs/, with an interactive API reference; make docs-serve to preview).

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
Scripts in eval/ write raw results with the environment and commit id to eval/results/.

Script Measures eval/quality.py origin-grouping precision/recall vs ground truth, evidence rules (A15), clarification questions, prompt injection eval/seeded_errors.py validator detection of seeded errors (hand-written E3 set and errors generated from a pipeline report) eval/drills.py failure drills: provider down, invalid JSON, validator independence, budget cap, Redis down, PostgreSQL down, worker kill, stuck threads eval/report_time.py report time and admission for a burst of 10 requests on real workers perf/run_load.py NFR1 read load: 50 Locust users for 3 minutes

Results and their limits are summarised in the implementation report. All quality figures describe the simulator and the synthetic corpus, not Claude on live news.

docs.title: Deploy with Docker Compose
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env        # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, KEY_PEPPER (and GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD for monitoring)
docker compose up -d --build                         # postgres, redis, migrate, api, worker-llm, worker-cpu, scheduler
docker compose run --rm api masader key create "Admin" admin@example.org admin
docker compose --profile monitoring up -d            # Prometheus :9090, Grafana :3000, Jaeger :16686
MASADER_DOMAIN=example.org docker compose --profile edge up -d    # Caddy with automatic TLS

The API listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 only; publish it through the edge profile. Behind a TLS-intercepting proxy, build with docker build --secret id=ca,src=/path/to/ca.crt --network host ..

docs.title: Distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry)
docs.text: Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://jaeger:4318 in .env and start the monitoring profile. Each report then has one trace in Jaeger (http://127.0.0.1:16686): the HTTP request, the Celery publish and run span of each of the eight stages, every database query, and an llm.complete / llm.call span per model call with GenAI attributes (model, input and output tokens, outcome, fallback, estimated cost; never prompt or source text). The X-Trace-Id response header and the trace_id in error bodies are the trace id to search for. Tracing is off when the variable is empty. Code: masader/telemetry.py; recorded run: eval/results/tracing.json and docs/tracing-jaeger.png.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause and fix ValueError: timer order violated at start A timer env variable breaks the required order; restore the defaults or keep the order above. MODEL_MODE=live needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Set the key in .env, or use MODEL_MODE=simulated. /readyz returns 503 PostgreSQL or Redis is not reachable; the JSON says which. make services, check DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL. POST /v1/requests returns 503 queue_unavailable Redis is down; nothing was stored, resend later with the same Idempotency-Key. 429 busy with Retry-After: 60 Six reports are already in progress (admission limit); retry after the given seconds. 429 rate_limited The key's hourly request limit is used up. 429 budget_exhausted The purpose's AI budget for the period is spent (budgets table). Report stays waiting_provider Both models failed; the stage retries every 60 s and the circuit breaker re-tests after 60 s. Report goes to in_review The validator removed too much, a stage failed twice, no independent validator model was available, or the topic is sensitive; a reviewer decides at /v1/review/{id}. could not open extension control file ... vector The database lacks pgvector; use the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image. Arabic and English copies are not grouped Expected with EMBEDDER=hashing; use fastembed where the model can be downloaded. pip install fails TLS behind a proxy Set PIP_CERT to your proxy CA, or use the Docker build secret above.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
masader/            application package
  api/              FastAPI app, models, planner, minimal UI
  pipeline/         Celery app, stage protocol (kit.py), stages/, retention
  gateway/          model client, budget reservation, providers (live + simulated)
  rules/            evidence rules and assertion checks (rules-1.1.1)
  processing/       ingest, retrieval, embeddings, origin groups, text, redaction
  connectors/       GDELT, RSS, World Bank, synthetic fixture
  render/           Jinja2 brief template
  simulated/        heuristic stand-in for the model roles (labelled)
  store/            database pool, SQL migrations, object store
config/             routing, budgets, rules, sources, gazetteer
prompts/            versioned role prompts used in live mode
data/sample/        synthetic corpus and its generator
tests/              unit, integration, ai, e2e
eval/               evaluation scripts and results/
perf/               Locust load test
ops/                Prometheus, Grafana, Caddy configuration
docs/               architecture diagram, deviations, OpenAPI contract, report material

docs.title: Licence and responsible use
docs.text: MIT. Briefs are AI-generated summaries of what sources report; read the cited evidence before relying on a finding. The input policy refuses requests to profile private individuals.

docs.title: Statement on AI-generated content
docs.text:
• The Masader system itself uses AI models at run time (planner, extractor, verifier, writer, splitter, support check). In this build those calls are answered by a deterministic heuristic simulator; no output presented in the report or demo is a real model output, and this is labelled wherever it appears.
  • No measurement in the report was invented or estimated without saying so. Cost figures are estimates at list prices on estimated token counts and are labelled as estimates.
  • No credentials are included in the repository.
  • The demo videos were recorded automatically from the running system with a script (perf/demo/record_demo.js, perf/demo/record_narrated.js). The narration in masader_demo_narrated.mp4 is a synthetic text-to-speech voice (Pico TTS) reading a script written with Claude; it is not MRA's voice.

docs.title: Demo video script (about 8 minutes)
docs.text:
Recorded by Mariam Alshamsi (MRA). Screen: a terminal on the left, a browser on the right. Say clearly at the start, and leave visible on screen, that model outputs in this demo come from the heuristic simulator and the news items are a synthetic corpus.

Time Show Say 0:00–0:40 Title slide: "Masader: evidence-labelled research briefs" and the architecture diagram (docs/architecture.png) "Masader turns a question about recent events into a one-page brief in which every finding says how well it is supported and links to its sources. This is the implementation of my proposal and architecture. In this demo the AI model calls are simulated, because no API key was available, and the sources are a synthetic set of 37 news items. Everything else runs for real." 0:40–1:30 Terminal: docker ps (postgres, redis), then make migrate seed, make run, make worker, make beat in three panes "The system is a FastAPI service, Celery workers for CPU and model stages, PostgreSQL with pgvector, and Redis. Seeding loads the source register, the budgets and the synthetic corpus." 1:30–2:00 python -m masader.cli key create "Demo" demo@example.org admin; point at "shown once" "API keys are stored only as an HMAC; the key is shown once." 2:00–3:00 Browser at http://127.0.0.1:8000: paste key, keep the Hormuz example, press Request brief; the clarification question appears "The planner checks the request first: ambiguous names, too broad, too little evidence, or asking for predictions. Here it asks one question with a default, so I can just send it." 3:00–4:00 Status line counting stages 1→8; then the brief in the sandboxed frame. Scroll: simulated banner, key findings with labels, a disputed finding, "insufficient" figure, what to watch "Eight stages run in order. Each finding has a label: corroborated means at least two independent origins, here including an official statement. The insurance premium is disputed, 0.5 versus 0.7 percent, so the brief gives both versions. The old 6-hour reporting figure was superseded, so it is labelled insufficient and kept out of the findings." 4:00–4:40 Click a source link / show the evidence passage; show that the injection item (newsroundup ... injection) is not cited "Every finding links to the exact passage. One corpus item contains a prompt injection that says traffic doubled; it never reaches the brief." 4:40–5:20 Terminal: curl .../v1/reports/<id> JSON, versions with sim: model names; curl -X POST .../publish with a reviewer key; open /r/<id> "Reports are private until a reviewer publishes them. The JSON records every model and prompt version; in simulated mode the names start with sim." 5:20–6:20 Terminal: run pytest -q tests/e2e -k killed or show its log; then eval/results/drills.json summary "Reliability: each stage takes a lease and commits fenced on it. In this test I kill a worker with SIGKILL in the middle of a stage; the reaper notices the expired lease and the report is still delivered exactly once. The drills also stop Redis and PostgreSQL and inject provider outages." 6:20–7:30 eval/results numbers on screen: tests passed, coverage, A15 20/20, dedup precision 1.0, seeded errors 73% vs 95% target, report time, load test p95 "Here are the measured results against the targets. Some targets are met. The validator caught 73 percent of seeded errors, below the 95 percent target, because the support check here is a simple lexical simulator; with the real model this must be measured again. Arabic and English copies are not grouped because the offline embedder has no cross-lingual meaning." 7:30–8:00 docs/deviations.md and docs/traceability.md "Every deviation from the architecture is listed with its reason, and the traceability matrix links each requirement to code, tests and results. Thank you."

Checklist before recording: fresh make seed; create keys in advance and keep them off screen; close any window that shows .env; zoom the terminal to 125%.

docs.title: Deviations from Architecture v1.2
docs.text:
Every place where the implementation differs from the Technical Architecture Deliverable v1.2 (28 Oct 2026) or the Proposal (19 Oct 2026), with the reason and what it costs. "Simulated" or "substituted" items are also labelled in the code, the API (model_mode, sim: model names) and every generated brief.

ID Area Architecture v1.2 Implementation Why Effect / what it costs D-01 Model calls Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 through the Anthropic SDK MODEL_MODE=simulated (default): a deterministic heuristic simulator in masader/simulated/heuristics.py answers every role, reading the real stage payloads and returning schema-valid JSON. MODEL_MODE=live calls the Anthropic API with the same gateway. No API key was available while building. All quality numbers measure the simulator, not Claude. The live path is implemented and unit-tested against a fake SDK client, but has not been run against the real API. Model names are recorded as sim:<model>; briefs show a "simulated" banner. D-02 Embeddings paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 (ONNX, fastembed) HashingEmbedder (feature hashing, 384 dims) is the default; the fastembed class exists behind the same interface but is optional and untested Model files could not be downloaded in the build environment No cross-lingual similarity: Arabic and English versions of one story are not grouped by embedding (dedup recall 0.20 on cross-language pairs, 1.00 on same-language pairs). D-03 Source data Live GDELT, ~20 RSS feeds, World Bank Connectors for all three are implemented and unit-tested on recorded responses; evaluation uses a synthetic 37-item corpus with fictional "(fixture)" outlets and a 12-row World Bank fixture No outbound access to the sources from the build environment; a fixed corpus is also needed for repeatable evaluation Results describe the synthetic corpus. Live ingestion is off unless LIVE_SOURCES=1. D-04 Language detection langdetect 1.0.9 Script-share rule (Arabic vs Latin letters) Only Arabic and English are in scope; avoids a dependency Other languages are reported as other. D-05 PII redaction Presidio pattern recognizers Hand-written regular expressions for the same kinds (email, phone, IBAN, payment card, Emirates ID, passport number), plus policy patterns for credentials, confidentiality markings and profiling of private individuals Presidio pulls spaCy into the image for regexes Names and street addresses are not detected (as with Presidio's pattern-only mode). D-06 Article extraction trafilatura 2.3 Feed summaries / HTML stripped with the standard library Dependency and network constraints Full-page extraction is not available for live RSS items. D-07 Report schema sections held plain strings (C.3) Each section holds sentences {text, findings[]} that reference finding ids The validator and the reader both need to know which finding a sentence rests on API contract change from C.3; recorded in docs/openapi.v1.json and tested. D-08 Evidence rules rules-1.1.0 rules-1.1.1 The reason text had a stray comma ("2 independent origins, (best tier A)") Wording only; labels unchanged (A15 still 20/20). D-09 Migrations Alembic Plain numbered SQL files applied by masader migrate with a schema_migrations table The schema is SQL-first (pgvector, CHECK constraints); one less framework No auto-generated down migrations; rollback is restore-from-backup (as NFR12 already planned). D-10 Migration 0002 — Adds sources.official, correction resolution columns, reports.stats, reports.trace_id, claims.item_id, requests.plan, two indexes Needed by the rules (official source), corrections workflow, and to keep the planner's plan with the request Additive only. D-11 Near-duplicate test MinHash LSH Exact Jaccard over word shingles inside the request window The window holds at most a few hundred items, so exact comparison is cheap and has no false negatives from hashing Would need LSH for a much larger window. D-12 Token counting Anthropic token-count endpoint characters / 2 estimate for reservation and simulated cost No API key Cost figures are estimates at list prices on estimated tokens (about US$0.26 per report). Reservation stays conservative. D-13 Exports Presigned S3 URLs JSON/HTML exports are served by the API from the database/object store, with an ETag Keeps the key check on every download; no S3 in the build environment Slightly more API load per export (measured in the load test). D-14 Object store S3 Local directory store (default) and an S3 class behind the same interface (boto3; not exercised against AWS) No AWS account — D-15 Deployment Docker Compose on one EC2 host, Route 53 health check compose.yaml with the same services plus monitoring and edge profiles; image built locally; not deployed to a cloud host No cloud account in scope for the build NFR3 availability cannot be measured. D-16 CI/CD GitHub Actions with gitleaks, image push Resolved on 23 Nov 2026. CI on GitHub Actions (gitleaks, pre-commit, ruff, bandit, pip-audit, tests with an 80% coverage gate, OpenAPI diff, image build, Trivy, SBOM) passes on main; the image is pushed to GitHub Container Registry by the release workflow (v1.0.0). Until then there was no GitHub repository — https://github.com/maryamrra90-create/masader/actions; release v1.0.0. D-17 Metrics Exporters on api, worker-llm (9101), worker-cpu (9102), node-exporter Only the API exposes /metrics (HTTP latency, request outcomes, queue lengths, reports by status, budget left) Worker exporters were not needed for the measured experiments Per-stage timings come from report_stages in PostgreSQL instead of Prometheus. D-18 Experiment tracking MLflow + DVC for frozen sets Frozen test cases are versioned in Git (eval/cases_e3.py, data/sample/); results are JSON files in eval/results/ with the commit id Small data; no tracking server No experiment UI. D-19 Stage 2 React app, Arabic output, topic area B, watched topics Not built (stage 2 by design) Out of scope for this deliverable The minimal HTML form at / is the only UI. D-20 Origin grouping Attribution verbs list Plain "said" added to the attribution verbs Corpus copies attributed with "said" were not grouped Slightly more attribution matches; precision stayed 1.0 on the corpus. D-21 Retrieval Hybrid score, no floor Hybrid score (0.5·cosine + 0.5·normalised ts_rank) with a cosine floor of 0.30 for items without a keyword match; stop words removed from the tsquery Hashing-embedding noise between unrelated texts reaches about 0.2, and stop words matched every item Tuned on the development corpus; must be re-checked with the real embedder. D-22 Claim merging Merge near-identical claims Merge only when the claims' numbers are equal Two claims that differ only in a figure (6 vs 4 hours) were merged, hiding a superseded figure Fewer merges; a changed figure stays visible as its own claim. D-23 Simulator limit — The simulated Writer leaves Arabic claims out of the brief The simulator cannot translate Arabic-only evidence does not appear in simulated briefs; a real model would translate it. D-24 Retention Daily retention task (NFR9) masader.ops.retention (daily beat task and masader retention) purges full text and raw objects after sources.fulltext_days and AI call traces after 90 days As designed Log retention is left to the Docker log driver.

docs.title: Results that miss their targets
docs.text:
These are reported, not hidden; see the implementation report, Section 5.

  • Seeded errors caught by the validator: target ≥ 95%. Measured with the simulated support check: 60/82 = 73% (Wilson 95% CI 0.63–0.82) on errors generated from a pipeline report; 20/20 on the hand-written E3 set, which the heuristic was written against (optimistic).
  • Clarification: 5 of 8 cases asked the expected questions; the three misses are the "widen" question, because the hit count matches generic words.
  • Cross-language duplicate detection: recall 0.20 (hashing embedder, D-02).

docs.title: Engineering toolchain and AI use
docs.text:
Project: Masader, implementation deliverable · Repository: https://github.com/maryamrra90-create/masader (commit a1ae607, release v1.0.0)

This section lists every tool that the repository, its CI configuration, its pinned requirements, the Compose file and the recorded evaluation outputs show was actually used. Each entry says what the tool does in Masader, why it was chosen, and where the evidence is. Paths are relative to the repository root unless they start with architecture/ (the architecture submission package) or demo/ (the implementation package). Where a tool is wired in but was not exercised in this build, the entry says so; those are marked Integrated, not exercised.

The section has three parts, kept separate on purpose:

  • A. AI assistance used to build the project (what helped MRA write it)
  • B. AI inside the product (what Masader itself calls at run time)
  • C. Non-AI engineering tools (everything else)

docs.title: B.3 Gateway controls around the model
docs.text:
These are engineering controls Masader puts around every model call (all in masader/gateway/):

  • Schema validation of every reply with jsonschema; invalid JSON is retried, then sent to review (client.py ~158).
  • Circuit breaker per model, with fallback to the next model in the route (circuit.py, config/routing.yaml).
  • Budget reservation: cost is reserved before a call and settled after, so spend never passes the cap; checked by the budget_near_cap drill (budget.py, config/budgets.yaml, eval/results/drills.json).
  • Prompt-injection control: source text goes inside tagged <source> blocks with < and > escaped, so a source cannot close the block or open a fake one (providers.py, _source_block).
  • Versioned prompts as files (prompts/*.v1.0.md), so a prompt change is a reviewed diff.

docs.title: C.6 Tools used in the architecture validation experiments (E1–E3)
docs.text: The architecture deliverable (28 Oct 2026) measured its key decisions before implementation, with Docker 29.9 / Compose 5.6, PostgreSQL 16.15 + pgvector 0.8.7 (E1: 200,000 items, exact vs HNSW recall and latency), FastAPI + Celery + Redis (E2: async pipeline and failure drills), Locust (E2 read load), the pgvector Python adapter, NumPy and httpx, and an offline wheel folder so the E2 image builds without internet. Every measured number maps to a file in architecture/validation/MEASUREMENTS.md, with checksums in SHA256SUMS.

docs.title: Engineering practices these tools support
docs.text:
• Reproducibility: every dependency pinned; result files record commit, Python version and platform; the architecture package has a step-by-step REPRODUCE.md and SHA-256 checksums.
  • Shift-left security: secret scan of full history, SAST (Bandit, Ruff S, CodeQL), dependency audit (pip-audit), container and IaC scan (Trivy), all blocking in CI; pre-commit hooks locally; an SBOM per build and signed provenance per release; automated dependency updates (Dependabot); non-root container; secrets only from .env (.env.example committed, .env git-ignored).
  • Contract-first API: OpenAPI document committed and diffed in CI.
  • Reliability by design, tested: idempotency keys, late acknowledgement, time limits, circuit breakers, budget reservation, each with a drill that proves it.
  • Observability: the three pillars in one stack: metrics (Prometheus), alerts and dashboards (Grafana), and distributed traces (OpenTelemetry + Jaeger).
  • Honest AI evaluation: the simulator is labelled everywhere; live-model quality (M5) is reported as not measured.
